title: Lamingtons
description: Day-old sponge cut into cubes, dipped in a thin chocolate icing and rolled in coconut. Makes a 20 cm square tin's worth, which is sixteen generous squares.
notes: The overnight rest is not about flavour. A fresh sponge is too tender to survive being dipped and it disintegrates into the icing bowl, which is by far the most common way this goes wrong.

steps.text: Beat the eggs and caster sugar until the mixture is pale and thick enough to hold a ribbon on the surface for three seconds.
steps.tip: Every bit of the rise comes from here. Under-whipped eggs give a flat, tight crumb and no amount of raising agent puts it back.

steps.text: Fold in the self-raising flour in three additions, then the melted butter, the milk and the vanilla extract.
steps.tip: Fold, do not stir. Each stroke past the point where the flour disappears costs you height.

steps.text: Pour into a lined square tin and bake until the sponge springs back when pressed in the middle.
Cool the sponge completely in the tin, then wrap it and leave it overnight.
steps.tip: A day-old sponge cuts into clean cubes and holds together in the icing. This step is the whole difference between neat lamingtons and a bowl of chocolate crumbs.

steps.text: Trim the crusts and cut the sponge into sixteen even cubes.
Whisk the icing sugar, cocoa powder and melted butter with the boiling water until the icing runs off a spoon in a sheet.
steps.tip: Thinner than looks right. Thick icing drags the sponge apart and sets in ugly ridges.

steps.text: Spread the desiccated coconut in a wide tray. Drop each cube into the icing, lift it out on two forks, let it drip, then roll it through the coconut.
steps.tip: Two forks, one cube at a time, and coconut-side hand kept dry. Wet fingers in the coconut tray turn it into a clumped mess within four cubes.

steps.text: Set the coated cubes on a rack until the icing has firmed up.
steps.tip: If the icing thickens while you work, sit its bowl over a pan of hot water for a minute rather than adding more liquid.
